flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk in Chromium at 1440x900 (DSF 1) and 390x844 (DSF 3). The most prominent first-screen action at 1440 is the red (rgb 196,58,47) a.btn-primary.js-beta 'Open the beta editor' in the hero (222x57 at top 517), repeated in the header (169x38) and the final band 'Go stitch something you took yourself.'. Clicking each of the three at both widths: no navigation (URL stays file:///.../index.html), no new page, no console error; the handler (app.js, CONFIG.BETA_URL '') calls preventDefault, scrolls to the on-page #editor 'Try it: a pattern you can edit' (scrollY 674 at 1440, 729 at 390), focuses canvas#pattern and only then shows the toast 'The beta is moving to its permanent address. Until then, the editor below is the real thing.' The label names a destination, the beta editor, that it does not reach: the page itself separates the two, in the FAQ 'Which threads does it use?' ('The editor on this page uses a short sample of the range ... the beta editor matches against the full catalogue') and 'What happens to my photo?' ('On this page, nothing leaves your browser ... The beta editor keeps your photo ...'). Nothing visible before the click says that the button only scrolls to the on-page demo. The hero lede says 'The pattern below is live — click it.' and the note says 'Free while in beta. Everything on this page runs in your browser', but neither tells the visitor that 'Open the beta editor' leads to the demo and not to the beta. The disclosure appears only in the toast after the click. This is the table's 'label names a destination it does not reach ("Read the docs" that scrolls the page)' case. No exemption in 'Does not count' applies: the brief supplied no address, which is why linking out is impossible, but it does not make a mislabelled scroll exempt; the real result is not stated before the visitor commits; and this is the primary action, not a secondary link.
